paragraphs.title: Opening: Praise and a Prayer for Salvation

answers: Because he is good and his mercy endureth for ever
easy.explanation: Verse 1 says, “O give thanks unto the LORD; for he is good: for his mercy endureth for ever.”
easy.q: Why should the LORD be thanked at the beginning of the psalm?

answers: Remember and visit him with salvation
easy.explanation: He prays, “Remember me, O LORD... O visit me with thy salvation.”
easy.q: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to do for him?

easy.explanation: He asks to rejoice “in the gladness of thy nation” and glory with God’s inheritance.
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist wish to rejoice?

answers: One who keeps judgment and does righteousness at all times
medium.explanation: The verse says, “Blessed are they that keep judgment, and he that doeth righteousness at all times.”
medium.q: What kind of person is called blessed in verse 3?

medium.explanation: In this context, “utter” means to speak, declare, or tell.
medium.q: What does “utter” mean in “Who can utter the mighty acts of the LORD?”

answers: So that he may share in the good and joy of God’s people
So that he may leave the people
So that he may rule the inheritance
medium.explanation: He asks to see the good of God’s chosen, rejoice with His nation, and glory with His inheritance.
medium.q: Why does the psalmist ask to be remembered by the LORD?

answers: From praise of the LORD to personal and communal prayer
From war to the building of a temple
challenge.explanation: The passage begins with thanksgiving and praise, then turns to a request for salvation and fellowship with God’s people.
challenge.q: What movement occurs in the opening verses?

answers: It is limited to special occasions
challenge.explanation: The phrase shows that righteousness is not restricted to one particular time.
challenge.q: What does “at all times” emphasize about doing righteousness?

answers: The psalmist wants to share in the praise and joy of God’s people
He wants to abandon the people
He wants to control the inheritance
challenge.explanation: He asks to participate in the good, gladness, and praise of the LORD’s people.
challenge.q: Why is the request to “glory with thine inheritance” also a request for belonging?

short_answers.question: Complete the phrase: “for he is good: for his mercy...”
short_answers.explanation: This is the conclusion of verse 1.

short_answers.question: What does the psalmist ask the LORD to visit him with?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 4 says, “O visit me with thy salvation.”

short_answers.question: Who are described as blessed?
short_answers.answer: They that keep judgment and do righteousness at all times
short_answers.explanation: This is the description in verse 3.

paragraphs.title: The Ancestors’ Sins and Salvation at the Sea of Reeds

easy.explanation: Verse 6 says, “We have sinned with our fathers.”
easy.q: With whom does the psalmist confess that Israel sinned?

answers: At the sea, even at the Red sea
easy.explanation: They provoked the LORD “at the sea, even at the Red sea.”
easy.q: Where did the fathers provoke the LORD?

answers: By making a covenant with them
By the LORD’s power at the Red sea
easy.explanation: The LORD rebuked the sea, led Israel through it, and saved them from their enemies.
easy.q: How were Israel saved from their enemies?

answers: They did not remember the multitude of his mercies
medium.explanation: The verse says they remembered not the multitude of God’s mercies.
medium.q: Why did the fathers provoke the LORD at the Red sea?

medium.explanation: Verse 12 says, “Then believed they his words; they sang his praise.”
medium.q: What did the people do after they believed the LORD’s words?

answers: A condition of inward weakness or lack after granting their request
Leading them away from the wilderness
medium.explanation: The phrase describes the harmful result of receiving what they desired.
medium.q: What does “sent leanness into their soul” describe?

answers: Sin, salvation, and then renewed forgetfulness or sin
challenge.explanation: The people forgot God, were saved at the sea, and soon forgot His works again and lusted in the wilderness.
challenge.q: What repeated pattern appears in this passage?

answers: That his mighty power might be known
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 explains that God acted so “that he might make his mighty power to be known.”
challenge.q: Why did the LORD save Israel “for his name’s sake”?

answers: They moved from faith and praise to forgetfulness, impatience, and testing God
They moved from slavery to kingship
They moved from the land to the wilderness without sin
challenge.explanation: After believing and singing, they soon forgot God’s works, waited not for His counsel, and tempted Him.
challenge.q: What contrast follows the people’s song of praise?

short_answers.question: What did Israel forget in Egypt?
short_answers.answer: The multitude of the LORD’s mercies
short_answers.explanation: Verse 7 says they remembered not the multitude of His mercies.

short_answers.question: What happened to the Red sea when the LORD rebuked it?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 9 says, “and it was dried up.”

short_answers.question: What did the people do after believing God’s words?

paragraphs.title: Rebellions in the Wilderness and the Golden Calf

easy.explanation: Verse 16 says, “They envied Moses also in the camp, and Aaron the saint of the LORD.”
easy.q: Whom did the people envy in the camp?

easy.explanation: The earth opened and swallowed Dathan and covered the company of Abiram.
easy.q: What did the earth do to Dathan and Abiram?

answers: A calf and a molten image
easy.explanation: They made a calf at Horeb and worshipped the molten image.
easy.q: What did Israel make at Horeb?

answers: The earth swallowed some and fire burned the wicked
medium.explanation: The passage describes the earth swallowing Dathan and Abiram and fire burning the wicked.
medium.q: What happened to Dathan, Abiram, and the wicked company?

answers: They exchanged the glory of God for an idol
They added glory to the LORD
They exchanged the wilderness for a land
medium.explanation: They replaced the worship of God with the image of an ox that eats grass.
medium.q: What does it mean that they “changed their glory” into the likeness of an ox?

answers: It turned away God’s wrath so the people were not destroyed
It caused the calf to be made
It brought the people back to Egypt
medium.explanation: Moses stood before the LORD “to turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them.”
medium.q: What was the effect of Moses standing in the breach?

answers: Both express rebellion against God’s appointed order and worship
Both concern deliverance at the sea
Both concern a request for food
challenge.explanation: The passage presents envy of God’s servants and the replacement of God’s glory with an idol as acts of rebellion.
challenge.q: What connects the rebellion against Moses and Aaron with the golden calf?

answers: He stands in the breach and intercedes to prevent the people’s destruction
He leads the worship of the calf
challenge.explanation: Moses is described as God’s chosen one who stood before Him in the breach.
challenge.q: What role does Moses play in this passage?

answers: They show the greatness of what the people forgot
They show the power of the calf
They describe the success of Israel’s enemies
challenge.explanation: The people forgot the God who had done great and wondrous works in Egypt and at the Red sea.
challenge.q: Why are God’s great works mentioned before the account of the calf?

short_answers.question: What was Aaron called in the passage?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 16 calls Aaron “the saint of the LORD.”

short_answers.question: What did the calf resemble?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 20 describes the idol as the similitude of an ox that eats grass.

short_answers.question: Who stood in the breach before the LORD?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 23 identifies Moses as God’s chosen servant who interceded.

paragraphs.title: The Spies, Baal Peor, and the Waters of Meribah

easy.explanation: Verse 24 says, “they despised the pleasant land.”
Phinehas stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stayed.
They angered the LORD at the waters of strife.
easy.q: What did the people do at the waters of strife?

answers: They were overthrown in the wilderness and scattered
medium.explanation: The LORD lifted up His hand to overthrow them in the wilderness and scatter their seed among the nations.
medium.q: What resulted from Israel’s unbelief concerning the land?

medium.explanation: To murmur means to complain or speak with discontent.
medium.q: What does “murmured in their tents” mean?

answers: The people joined themselves to Baal-peor and ate sacrifices of the dead
The people went to war in Canaan
medium.explanation: Their idolatry and participation in those sacrifices provoked the LORD and brought the plague.
medium.q: Why did the plague come after Baal-peor?

answers: Both reject the word and voice of the LORD
Both concern the song of the Levites
challenge.explanation: The people believed not God’s word and hearkened not unto His voice.
challenge.q: What do unbelief concerning the land and refusal to heed the LORD have in common?

answers: He stood up and executed judgment, and the plague was stopped
challenge.explanation: The passage connects Phinehas’s action with the stopping of the plague and calls it righteousness.
challenge.q: Why was Phinehas’s action counted as righteousness?

answers: It went ill with him for their sakes
He became king over the nations
challenge.explanation: Verse 32 says, “so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes.”
challenge.q: What happened to Moses because of the waters of strife?

short_answers.question: What did the people refuse to believe?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 24 says, “they believed not his word.”

short_answers.question: What did the people provoke Moses to do?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 33 gives this consequence of provoking his spirit.

paragraphs.title: Sins in the Land and Punishment through Foreign Nations

answers: Destroy them as the LORD commanded
easy.explanation: Verse 34 says they did not destroy the nations concerning whom the LORD commanded them.
easy.q: What did Israel fail to do to the nations in the land?

easy.explanation: They were mingled among the heathen and learned their works.
easy.q: What did Israel learn from the heathen?

answers: The hand of the heathen and their enemies
The hand of the priests in the wilderness
easy.explanation: The LORD gave them into the hand of the heathen, who ruled over them.
easy.q: Into whose hand were Israel given because of their sins?

answers: They learned their works and served their idols
They immediately returned to the wilderness
medium.explanation: They learned the works of the nations and served their idols, which became a snare.
medium.q: What resulted from Israel’s mixture with the heathen?

answers: Something that traps or brings danger
medium.explanation: The idols became a snare, meaning a dangerous trap that ensnared the people.
medium.q: What is a “snare” in this passage?

answers: As acts that polluted the land with innocent blood
medium.explanation: The passage says that shedding this innocent blood polluted the land.
medium.q: How are the sacrifices of sons and daughters described?

answers: Mixing with the nations led to sin, judgment, oppression, and repeated deliverance
Worship of the LORD led to captivity
challenge.explanation: Israel adopted pagan practices, was judged and oppressed, yet the LORD repeatedly delivered them and remembered His covenant.
challenge.q: What is the main chain of cause and effect in this passage?

answers: He repeatedly rescued them despite their rebellion
challenge.explanation: The verse emphasizes repeated deliverance even though the people continued to provoke Him.
challenge.q: What does “Many times did he deliver them” reveal about the LORD?

answers: It explains God’s mercy and renewed compassion after judgment
It erases all the people’s sins
challenge.explanation: The LORD remembered His covenant and regarded their affliction according to the multitude of His mercies.
challenge.q: Why does the remembrance of the covenant change the direction of the passage?

short_answers.question: What did the idols become to Israel?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 36 says, “which were a snare unto them.”

short_answers.question: What did Israel sacrifice to devils?
What did the LORD remember for Israel?
short_answers.explanation: Verse 45 says, “he remembered for them his covenant.”

paragraphs.title: Prayer for Gathering and the Closing Praise

answers: Save them and gather them from among the heathen
easy.explanation: Verse 47 says, “Save us, O LORD our God, and gather us from among the heathen.”
easy.q: What does the people ask the LORD to do?

answers: To give thanks unto God’s holy name and triumph in his praise
To learn the works of the heathen
easy.explanation: They seek gathering so they may give thanks and rejoice in the LORD’s praise.
easy.q: Why do they ask to be gathered?

easy.explanation: The psalm closes with, “and let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the LORD.”
easy.q: How does the people respond at the end?

answers: Salvation and gathering will enable the people to give thanks
medium.explanation: The request for salvation and gathering is made so the people can give thanks unto God’s holy name.
medium.q: What connection does verse 47 make between salvation and thanksgiving?

answers: To rejoice and glory in praising the LORD
medium.explanation: The phrase expresses joyful participation in the LORD’s praise.
medium.q: What does “to triumph in thy praise” mean in context?

answers: Both contain thanksgiving and praise for the LORD’s enduring mercy
The beginning concerns war and the ending concerns kingship
The beginning rejects praise and the ending accepts it
medium.explanation: The psalm opens with thanksgiving because God is good and ends with blessing and praise.
medium.q: How does the ending connect with the beginning of the psalm?

answers: From distress and scattering to salvation, gathering, and thanksgiving
From salvation to forgetting the LORD
challenge.explanation: The people ask to be saved and gathered so they can thank and praise the LORD.
challenge.q: What is the main movement in the final prayer?

answers: It ends with communal praise and public agreement
It adds another account of sin
challenge.explanation: The blessing of the LORD is answered by all the people with “Amen” and praise.
challenge.q: Why does the conclusion include both a blessing and the people’s response?

answers: Even after sin and scattering, God’s people seek salvation based on mercy and covenant
The people no longer need salvation
The heathen are the source of salvation
challenge.explanation: After recounting sin, judgment, mercy, and covenant, the people ask for salvation and gathering so they may praise God.
challenge.q: What broad idea from the psalm is summarized in the request for gathering?

short_answers.question: From whom does the people ask to be gathered?
What do they desire to give thanks unto?
short_answers.explanation: They ask to be gathered “to give thanks unto thy holy name.”

short_answers.question: What does all the people say at the end?
short_answers.explanation: The final verse says, “let all the people say, Amen. Praise ye the LORD.”
